lesson_title: Two Trolleys at the Scrap-Yard Gate
hook_text: One trolley carries cans from the bins. The other carries copper with the plastic burned off. Only one should be paid.
clip_script: Metal never wears out. A steel can melts into new steel; copper melts into new wire. Recycling saves ore, saves huge amounts of energy, and keeps metal out of landfill, so a dealer pays for scrap by the kilogram. Who brings it? Mostly gleaners, people who push trolleys through town on refuse day, pulling cans and wire from bins. Tens of thousands of them, doing honest, skilled work. Now the other trolley: thick copper cable with the insulation burned off. That came from a live line somewhere. A suburb is dark tonight, or a train has stopped, or a manhole is open on a pavement. The law says the dealer must record every seller and refuse metal like this, and if the dealer buys it, the dealer is guilty too. The magnet crane sorts the metal. The dealer sorts the people.
visual_style: Whiteboard flow from bin to mill to new can; a trolley figure walking; a cable with burn marks and a dark street beyond it.
mood: Respectful and serious, two sides of one trade.
pacing: Brisk recycling loop, warm pause on the gleaner, slow and firm on the stolen cable.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and draw the recycling chain with the crane marked on it.
